top_items.title: Sony Cancels Live-Service PS5 Game Fairgames, But No Layoffs
top_items.summary: Sony has canceled the upcoming live-service shooter Fairgame$, but there will be no job cuts connected to the game's closure. This is according to a report from Bloomberg today. The game was in the works at Haven Studios in Montreal, a team founded by former Assassin's Creed veteran Jade Raymond. She left the studio back in 2023 , and Fairgame$ was delayed to 2026 at the time. Now the game is scrapped entirely. According to the report, Haven "reworked" the Fairgame$ concept several times in the past three years. The studio was reportedly planning to re-reveal it with a new name. Going forward, Haven staff will support other PlayStation projects, the report said. You can watch the original CGI reveal trailer for Fairgame$ below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l1Jp4K02L1I Fairgame$ was officially canceled following a playtest that didn't show strong results. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in a memo seen by Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Creative director Mathieu Leduc said in a blog post that Haven was founded with the goal of making games that its staffers wanted to play, and that’s why the team chose a competitive multiplayer game. “Fairgame$ came from a desire to create a new type of PvP game with emergent sandbox gameplay. We want to deliver a fresh multiplayer experience that rewards creativity and mastery and delivers surprising stories each and every time you play,” Leduc said. “In a nutshell, this is a thrilling competitive heist game where you join an underground movement to rob the ultra-rich and rebalance the scales,” Leduc said. As you can see in the announcement trailer, Fairgame$ has players going after billionaires who have “too much money and too much power.” In the trailer, we see a squad of players infiltrating some kind of compound, working together to take down security guards with the apparent aim of sticking it to the man. “Fairgame$ will give you an opportunity to break the rules as a modern-day Robin Hood, a thrill seeker, or just someone who wants to collect cool loot,” Leduc said. “Trespass inside forbidden locations around the world, fill your pockets like a kid in a candy store and unravel the nefarious plans of untouchable billionaires.” Back when Fairgame$ was announced in 2023, Sony was in the midst of a huge push and investment into the live-service market. At one point in time, Sony wanted to release 12 live-service games over the coming years (alongside its commitment to single-player games). However, in May 2023, Sony announced that it was halving its planned live-service game output , with management stressing it wanted to focus on quality over quantity. After this announcement, Naughty Dog’s The Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled in December 2023. At the beginning of 2024, though, Sony found its biggest success to date in the live-service market with Helldivers 2–the game went on to smash sales records and become the No. 3 overall best-selling game of 2024 in the US. In July 2024, Sony’s Destiny developer Bungie announced mass layoffs and major structural changes . A month later, Sony launched the multiplayer game Concord. It had such a dismal performance out of the gate that Sony quickly took the game offline and refunded all players . Its developer, Firewalk, was later closed. At the end of 2024, Sony confirmed that it canceled multiple projects, including a live-service God of War and another live-service title from Bend. It was reported in 2023 that PlayStation boss Jim Ryan, who left Sony in 2024, had a mandate that Sony’s teams should make more games-as-a-service titles . A number of PlayStation developers were reportedly upset with this, and the blame was said to have fallen not on Ryan but Connie Booth, one of the most important and veteran PlayStation developers, leading to her eventual departure. Another former PlayStation boss, Shuhei Yoshida, said the chance of finding success in the competitive live-service market was “small,” but his replacement, Hermen Hulst, was given the resources to fund both single-player games and live-service titles at the same time. However, had Yoshida stayed in that role, he said he would have “tried to resist” the push into the live-service market. He joked, “That’s one of the reasons they removed me.”

items.summary: Reform UK leader in the Senedd, Helen Jenner, backs Joe Martin after his ban Here are some more comments on the report for the Casey commission released today looking at how social care is run in England. (See 9.56am .) This is from Natasha Curry, deputy director of research at the Nuffield Trust and one of the report’s authors. Compared to the other countries we looked at, the governance of England’s social care system is confused and complex. Overlapping and unclear roles leave dangerous uncertainty around who is responsible for important decisions, contributing to the inertia around reform England has struggled with for decades. The serious consequences of this were laid bare during the Covid pandemic. The system for governing adult social care in England has evolved haphazardly and with little clear planning. That has been exacerbated by successive governments ducking politically unpalatable decisions for decades. That has scattered responsibility for the sector across and outside government in a way that few would design from scratch. This report makes for sober reading of how adult social care and those who rely on it have been systematically failed. The fragmentation we see today is what happens when there is a total absence of political leadership to ensure the sector is well-funded and provides equitable access to care. [Burnham] struggled to dampen splits among cabinet ministers, which were first revealed by The i Paper , who used the meeting to express differing views on the future relationship with Brussels. items.summary: ‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’ Is this an opportunity for a new America? One can sense the ambition of the bumper new crop of Democrats ushered to power last week, calling for support for programs for children and their parents; emphatically endorsing the long-held dream of Medicare for All. The project includes rolling back Donald Trump ’s cuts to Medicaid and food stamps, and restoring subsidies for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act that Republicans allowed to expire. items.title: Sony Cancels Live-Service PS5 Game Fairgames, But No Layoffs
items.summary: Sony has canceled the upcoming live-service shooter Fairgame$, but there will be no job cuts connected to the game's closure. This is according to a report from Bloomberg today. The game was in the works at Haven Studios in Montreal, a team founded by former Assassin's Creed veteran Jade Raymond. She left the studio back in 2023 , and Fairgame$ was delayed to 2026 at the time. Now the game is scrapped entirely. According to the report, Haven "reworked" the Fairgame$ concept several times in the past three years. The studio was reportedly planning to re-reveal it with a new name. Going forward, Haven staff will support other PlayStation projects, the report said. You can watch the original CGI reveal trailer for Fairgame$ below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l1Jp4K02L1I Fairgame$ was officially canceled following a playtest that didn't show strong results. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in a memo seen by Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Creative director Mathieu Leduc said in a blog post that Haven was founded with the goal of making games that its staffers wanted to play, and that’s why the team chose a competitive multiplayer game. “Fairgame$ came from a desire to create a new type of PvP game with emergent sandbox gameplay. We want to deliver a fresh multiplayer experience that rewards creativity and mastery and delivers surprising stories each and every time you play,” Leduc said. “In a nutshell, this is a thrilling competitive heist game where you join an underground movement to rob the ultra-rich and rebalance the scales,” Leduc said. As you can see in the announcement trailer, Fairgame$ has players going after billionaires who have “too much money and too much power.” In the trailer, we see a squad of players infiltrating some kind of compound, working together to take down security guards with the apparent aim of sticking it to the man. “Fairgame$ will give you an opportunity to break the rules as a modern-day Robin Hood, a thrill seeker, or just someone who wants to collect cool loot,” Leduc said. “Trespass inside forbidden locations around the world, fill your pockets like a kid in a candy store and unravel the nefarious plans of untouchable billionaires.” Back when Fairgame$ was announced in 2023, Sony was in the midst of a huge push and investment into the live-service market. At one point in time, Sony wanted to release 12 live-service games over the coming years (alongside its commitment to single-player games). However, in May 2023, Sony announced that it was halving its planned live-service game output , with management stressing it wanted to focus on quality over quantity. After this announcement, Naughty Dog’s The Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled in December 2023. At the beginning of 2024, though, Sony found its biggest success to date in the live-service market with Helldivers 2–the game went on to smash sales records and become the No. 3 overall best-selling game of 2024 in the US. In July 2024, Sony’s Destiny developer Bungie announced mass layoffs and major structural changes . A month later, Sony launched the multiplayer game Concord. It had such a dismal performance out of the gate that Sony quickly took the game offline and refunded all players . Its developer, Firewalk, was later closed. At the end of 2024, Sony confirmed that it canceled multiple projects, including a live-service God of War and another live-service title from Bend. It was reported in 2023 that PlayStation boss Jim Ryan, who left Sony in 2024, had a mandate that Sony’s teams should make more games-as-a-service titles . A number of PlayStation developers were reportedly upset with this, and the blame was said to have fallen not on Ryan but Connie Booth, one of the most important and veteran PlayStation developers, leading to her eventual departure. Another former PlayStation boss, Shuhei Yoshida, said the chance of finding success in the competitive live-service market was “small,” but his replacement, Hermen Hulst, was given the resources to fund both single-player games and live-service titles at the same time. However, had Yoshida stayed in that role, he said he would have “tried to resist” the push into the live-service market. He joked, “That’s one of the reasons they removed me.”

items.title: GTA 6 Backflips Look Good Now, But There Could Be More To The Story
items.summary: A new Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer debuted today, November 10, and the video showed off a race car driver doing a backflip. The animation looks smoooth . That's notable because the Extended Look trailer that debuted back in August showed Jason doing a backflip and people online quickly roasted it for looking ... off. Other said it looked totally fine. Whatever the case, some are saying this new backflip animation being featured in the latest trailer is an example of Rockstar taking feedback seriously, but it could be more nuanced than that. That's a nice backflip. That's because it subsequently came to light that the backflip animation in GTA 6 is controlled by the player and isn't locked to one specific animation. However, we don't know who is doing the backflip in this newest clip. If the character in the trailer is an NPC, as people on Reddit are surmising , then the animation could have been motion-captured as opposed to being player-controlled, hence why it looks less janky. In any event, this backflip stuff becoming a "controversy," if you can even call it that, is yet another example of how ramped-up people are for GTA 6. People are so jazzed for the release that they are poring over even the smallest details, which you may never even notice when playing the game for yourself . https://twitter.com/TheCassiniGames/status/2120163720198594774 GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and preloading is live now. The game unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, and that means people in the US will be among the last in the world to play .

highlights: After surviving an early-stage battle against Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, polesitter George Russell led teammate Kimi Antonelli to Mercedes's 61st 1–2 finish.
Leclerc rounded out the podium for Ferrari ahead of teammate Lewis Hamilton; both drivers led for at least one lap during the Grand Prix.

His teammate, 19-year-old Kimi Antonelli, became the youngest Formula One polesitter, second-youngest Grand Prix winner and the first Italian to win a Grand Prix since Giancarlo Fisichella at the 2006 Malaysian Grand Prix.
Antonelli led a Mercedes 1–2 ahead of Russell and Lewis Hamilton, who achieved his maiden podium with Ferrari.
Antonelli took the lead of the Drivers' Championship for the first time in his career, becoming the youngest World Drivers' Championship leader at 19 years and 216 days.
Doing this, he also became Italy's first Drivers' Championship leader since Giancarlo Fisichella led the 2005 championship.
Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) then converted pole position for the Grand Prix to a win, Norris and Piastri completed the podium.
George Russell (Mercedes) converted pole position for the sprint event to a victory, following a short battle for the lead with Kimi Antonelli.
Russell also took pole position for the main race, where he and Antonelli again battled in the opening stages before a battery failure led to his first retirement since the 2024 British Grand Prix.
Antonelli inherited the lead and the race win, taking his fourth consecutive victory.

The podium was completed by Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and Max Verstappen (Red Bull), the latter taking his and Red Bull's first podium of the season, and Ford's first podium since Jordan Grand Prix's victory at the 2003 Brazilian Grand Prix.
It was held on 7 June 2026, at the Circuit de Monaco in Monaco, and was the sixth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship.
Converting pole position into a victory, Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) became the youngest driver to win the Monaco Grand Prix and the youngest to achieve a Grand Slam.
Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) and Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) completed the podium, marking Hadjar's first podium of the season.
Verstappen and Russell's Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli rounded out the podium.
Antonelli passed Hamilton to take his first sprint victory, while Lando Norris (McLaren) completed the podium.
Leclerc made a strong start to take the lead from Antonelli, while Hamilton also moved ahead of the Mercedes driver in the opening corners.
Antonelli later passed Hamilton and appeared set to challenge Leclerc for victory after making his sole pit stop on fresher tyres.
Still, a failure of his left-front wheel shield left him unable to turn the car normally and required two further pit stops.
Antonelli briefly lost the lead to Max Verstappen (Red Bull) on the opening lap and later to Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) after the latter benefited from a virtual safety car-assisted pit stop.
He recovered to pass Leclerc on lap 34 and won by just under two seconds, with Leclerc finishing second and Verstappen completing the podium.

Antonelli's championship rival and teammate George Russell retired following an opening-lap collision with Lewis Hamilton, enabling Antonelli to extend his championship lead to 45 points over Hamilton and 50 over Russell.
